{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_bdafaf102fc6444d8232b1ba","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-013: Pluggable Bead-CLI Backends — Three Upstreams, One Configurable Seam\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** Accepted — 2026-08-12 (proposed 2026-08-11; four drafts, see Revision History)\n4\t**Deciders:** operator (jedarden), via Claude Code\n5\t**Tracking:** see Phase 16 in `docs/plan/plan.md`; beads filed under label `bead-cli-backend`\n6\t\n7\t## Context\n8\t\n9\tNEEDLE must drive **three** independently-evolving bead CLIs, not one canonical tool plus legacy debris:\n10\t\n11\t| Priority | Backend | Binary | Upstream | Installed here |\n12\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n13\t| **primary** | **bead-rs** | `bead` | `git.ardenone.com/jedarden/bead-rs` | v0.1.3 (`85f36ac`) |\n14\t| **secondary** | **bead-forge** | `bf` | `git.ardenone.com/jedarden/bead-forge` | `~/.local/bin/bf`, v0.4.1 |\n15\t| **tertiary** | **beads_rust** | `br` | `github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust` | `~/.cargo/bin/br`, v0.1.28 |\n16\t| *(open world)* | any other | — | third-party, future, forks | not installed |\n17\t\n18\tThe priority column is an operator decision recorded in draft 4; see §7. It sets\n19\twhich backend the defaults favour and which descriptor is written first — it does\n20\t**not** reduce the others to second-class. All three stay first-class, and the\n21\topen-world row is a requirement, not a courtesy: NEEDLE must be able to drive a\n22\tbead CLI that did not exist when NEEDLE was compiled.\n23\t\n24\t(The original Go `beads` — `bd` v0.49.6, `~/go/bin/bd`, the common ancestor of all\n25\tthree — is the nearest concrete instance of that fourth row, and is why the three\n26\tdialects rhyme without matching.)\n27\t\n28\tThe immediate trigger is the `game-of-life` project in the **agent-sandbox** cluster, whose workspace is bead-rs-backed. Stock NEEDLE cannot drive it: a worker booted there fails at the first claim. But the investigation found the problem is broader than one missing backend, and that NEEDLE's *existing* handling of the two backends it nominally supports is already incorrect.\n29\t\n30\t### The seam is right; what leaks past it is not\n31\t\n32\t`trait BeadStore` (`src/bead_store/mod.rs:546`) already exists, is `Send + Sync`, and is what every consumer holds — `Arc<dyn BeadStore>` in `Worker` (`src/worker/mod.rs:306-308`), in `Claimer`, in every strand. Two impls already exist: `BrCliBeadStore` (`:701`) and `BfCliBeadStore` (`:1852`). Nothing in the worker or strand layer knows which CLI is underneath. **That part of the design is sound and does not change.**\n33\t\n34\tFour things leak past it.\n35\t\n36\t### 1. Binary resolution is hardcoded in five places, one of which bypasses the trait\n37\t\n38\t| Site | Behavior |\n39\t|---|---|\n40\t| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:758-775` | `BrCliBeadStore::discover` — chain `bf` → `~/.local/bin/bf` → `br` → `~/.local/bin/br` |\n41\t| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:1127-1136` | a **second**, independent `resolve_bf()` used only by `run_bf_batch` / `run_bf_claim` |\n42\t| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:1893-1902` | `BfCliBeadStore::discover` — a third copy |\n43\t| `src/worker/mod.rs:732-742` | boot-time version handshake, `which::which(\"bf\")` inline |\n44\t| `src/cli/mod.rs:3626-3632` | `needle doctor` preflight — `bf` else `br` else fail `\"no bead store CLI found on PATH (checked bf, br)\"` |\n45\t| `src/validation/predispatch.rs:128` | `run(workspace, \"bf\", &[\"show\", …])` — **bypasses `BeadStore` altogether** |\n46\t\n47\tThe first row is the load-bearing defect. **`BrCliBeadStore::discover` resolves `bf` first** — so the store that speaks beads_rust dialect is bound, by default, to the bead-forge binary. See §5.\n48\t\n49\t### 2. Three dialects, diverged from a common ancestor in three directions\n50\t\n51\tEnumerated from each installed binary's own `--help` on 2026-08-11. This is the matrix any backend abstraction has to absorb:\n52\t\n53\t| Operation | `br` 0.1.28 | `bf` 0.4.1 | `bead` 0.1.0 |\n54\t|---|---|---|---|\n55\t| atomic server-side claim | **absent** | `claim --model --harness --harness-version --assignee --json` | `claim --assignee --json --policy` (no velocity metadata) |\n56\t| transactional batch | **absent** | `batch --json '[…]'` | **absent** |\n57\t| create: description | `-d/--description` (**`--body` is a valid alias**) | `--description` only | `--description` only |\n58\t| create: labels | `-l/--labels` **comma-separated** | repeated `--label` | repeated `--label` |\n59\t| create: quiet ID | `--silent` | absent (bare ID on stdout) | absent (bare ID on stdout) |\n60\t| `dep add` | `<ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t blocks` — **2 positionals** | `<BLOCKER> --blocks <BLOCKED> -t` — **1 positional** | `<BLOCKED> <BLOCKER> --kind blocks` — **2 positionals** |\n61\t| `update --assignee` | present | **removed in 0.4.1** (`bf-1hmey`) | present, plus `--clear-assignee` |\n62\t| `sync --import-only` | bare | bare | requires `--input` + one of `--restore-into-empty`/`--merge` |\n63\t| ready frontier | `ready --json --limit` | `ready` | `list --ready` |\n64\t| `doctor --repair` | present | present | present |\n65\t| close reason | `-r/--reason` | `--reason` | `--reason` |\n66\t| machine-readable contract | `schema`; **`capabilities` + `robot-docs` as of 0.2.22** | `schema`, `robot-docs` | `capabilities --profile` |\n67\t\n68\tTwo structural facts fall out. **`bf` is the only backend with a transactional `batch`**, so it is the only one that can make mitosis atomic. **`bf` is the only backend that dropped `update --assignee`**, so it is the only one that *needs* `batch` for something as ordinary as claiming. Those two facts are the same fact, and together they set the bar for any backend abstraction: the backends do not differ only in flag spelling, they differ in which operations are single commands at all. A configuration format that captures only argv cannot express that difference — which is why the Decision below pairs argv templates with a per-operation *strategy*.\n69\t\n70\tNote also that `dep add`'s positional order agrees between `br` and `bead` (blocked first, blocker second) and `bf` is the outlier. Getting this backwards inverts every dependency edge rather than failing loudly — the one place in this ADR where a wrong guess is worse than a crash.\n71\t\n72\t### 3. The prompt hands the agent a hardcoded dialect\n73\t\n74\t`src/prompt/mod.rs` embeds `bf update` (`:56`), `bf close` (`:64`), and a whole `bf create` / `bf show` / `bf dep add` / `bf label add` block in the mitosis-split instructions (`:294-325`), with a test asserting the literal string (`:1066-1067`). An agent in the bead-rs sandbox is told to run a binary that is not installed there.\n75\t\n76\t### 4. Version-handshake logic is bead-forge-specific\n77\t\n78\t`check_bead_forge_version` / `run_version_handshake` (`:295-419`) parse bead-forge version strings to detect bf 0.2.0's `--limit 0` bug. Against `br --version` or `bead --version` this degrades to a warning, but the `--limit 999999` workaround it exists to justify is applied unconditionally at `:1357` and `:2094`.\n79\t\n80\t### 5. `BrCliBeadStore` is a *correct* beads_rust store bound to the wrong binary\n81\t\n82\tThis is the finding that reframes the rest. Checked against the real `br` 0.1.28 at `~/.cargo/bin/br`:\n83\t\n84\t```\n85\tcreate --title T --body B --json --silent --labels a,b      (:1550-1563)\n86\tdep add <blocked> <blocker> --type blocks                   (:1579)\n87\tsync --import-only                                          (:1706)\n88\tlist --json --limit 999999                                  (:1357)\n89\tdoctor --repair                                             (:1675)\n90\t```\n91\t\n92\t**Every one of these is valid beads_rust.** `--body` is a documented alias of `-d/--description`; `--silent` exists; `-l/--labels` is comma-separated; `dep add` takes two positionals with `-t` defaulting to `blocks`; `sync --import-only` is bare; `list` has `--json` and `--limit`. `BrCliBeadStore` is not stale, drifted, or wrong. It is a faithful beads_rust adapter.\n93\t\n94\tThe defect is that **`discover()` (`:758-775`) resolves `bf` before `br`**, so on this host — and on every fleet host, where `~/.local/bin/bf` is present — the beads_rust adapter sends beads_rust argv to the bead-forge binary, which rejects most of it. `bf 0.4.1 create` has no `--body`, no `--silent`, no `--labels`. `bf 0.4.1 dep add` takes one positional, not two.\n95\t\n96\tCompounding it, bf-only calls were grafted *into* the beads_rust store: `claim` (`:1428-1437`), `release` (`:1479-1486`), and `split` (`:1485`, `:1508`) all route through `bf batch` via the second resolver at `:1127`, and `claim_auto` shells to `bf claim` (`:1194-1220`). beads_rust has neither subcommand. So `BrCliBeadStore` is now a chimera: beads_rust argv for create/dep/sync/list, bead-forge argv for claim/release/split, and a resolver that picks whichever binary it finds first regardless of which half is being invoked.\n97\t\n98\tThere is exactly one genuine argv bug, and it is in the *other* store: `BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency` (`:2288`) emits two positionals, which is correct for `br` and `bead` but wrong for `bf`.\n99\t\n100\t**Consequence in production:** every worker path constructs `BrCliBeadStore` — `worker/mod.rs:1385`, `supervisor/mod.rs:214`, `strand/explore.rs:71`/`:450`, `strand/splice.rs:747`/`:839`/`:999`. `BfCliBeadStore` is built only in `cli/mod.rs:997` and `:3384`. So the fleet runs the chimera. `create_bead` fails with a clap parse error against `bf`, and through the trait's default `split_bead` (`:646-668`) that takes all of mitosis child creation with it.\n101\t\n102\t### 6. Descriptors must pin the version they were verified against\n103\t\n104\tThe `br` binary installed on this host is **v0.1.28, built 2026-03-29**. Upstream beads_rust is at **v0.2.22 (2026-08-06)** — roughly twenty releases and four months ahead. Every dialect fact in §2 was originally derived from the stale local binary.\n105\t\n106\tDownloading `br-0.2.22-linux_x86_64` from the GitHub release and re-probing confirms the dialect is stable across that gap on every point NEEDLE touches: `-d/--description` still carries `[alias: --body]`, `-l/--labels` is still comma-separated, `--silent` survives, `dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t` still takes two positionals, `update -s --assignee` is still present, and there is still no `claim` and no `batch`. That is luck, not design — and it is exactly the check a descriptor should force rather than leave to chance.\n107\t\n108\t0.2.22 does add subcommands: `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `capacity`, `coordination`, `gate`, `scheduler`, `vcs-status`. The first two matter here — **all three backends expose a capabilities-style contract surface**, so §4's negotiation is uniform rather than a bead-rs special case.\n109\t\n110\tTwo consequences for the design:\n111\t\n112\t- A descriptor carries `verified_against` (binary version) and the date it was checked. A fleet host running v0.1.28 while upstream ships v0.2.22 is normal; a descriptor that does not say which one it was written for is a guess.\n113\t- **bead-rs is under active development in agent-sandbox**, so its surface is a *moving* target, not a stale one: the local `~/bead-rs` is nine commits past the `fa30574` this ADR cites, including `20853cf`, which fixed a defect that bricked every fresh clone. Its descriptor must be verified against the binary the sandbox actually runs, and re-verified when that moves. Unlike `br` and `bf`, bead-rs publishes **no GitHub releases** — it is Forgejo-only — so there is no release artifact to pin to and the descriptor must name a commit.\n114\t\n115\t## Decision\n116\t\n117\t**One descriptor-driven `CliBeadStore`, with backends defined as data — not one hardcoded impl per upstream.**\n118\t\n119\tNEEDLE already solves this exact problem for AI agent harnesses and the bead layer should not invent a second answer. `AgentAdapter` (`src/dispatch/mod.rs`) is a serde struct; `load_adapters` (`:607-660`) merges `builtin_adapters()` (`:570-579`) with user YAML dropped in `~/.config/needle/adapters/`, user files overriding built-ins by name. Adding a new agent harness requires no recompile. The bead CLI gets the same shape.\n120\t\n121\t### 1. `BeadBackend` descriptors, loaded like adapters\n122\t\n123\tA `BeadBackend` is a serde struct describing one CLI: binary name, identity check, detection paths, per-operation argv templates, and a declared capability set. `builtin_bead_backends()` ships `beads_rust`, `bead-forge`, and `bead-rs` as **data, not code**; `load_bead_backends()` merges user YAML from `~/.config/needle/bead-backends/`, overriding built-ins by name. `bead_cli.backend` in config names one; `auto` detects.\n124\t\n125\tA fourth CLI — `bd`, a fork, a future tool — is a YAML file. No recompile, no NEEDLE release.\n126\t\n127\t### 2. Structural divergence is expressed as a *strategy* per operation, not as argv alone\n128\t\n129\tThis is the part a flat argv table cannot do, and the reason the first two drafts of this ADR reached for hardcoded impls. The backends differ in **which operations are single commands at all**: `bf` claims via one transactional `batch` because it has no `update --assignee`; `br` and `bead` claim via a plain `update`; `br` has no server-side `claim`, so `claim_auto` there is a two-step read-then-write with different race properties.\n130\t\n131\tSo each operation declares a strategy drawn from a small closed set, parameterized by argv templates:\n132\t\n133\t| Operation | Strategies | `br` | `bf` | `bead` |\n134\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n135\t| `claim` | `compare_and_set` \\| `batch_op` | compare_and_set | batch_op | compare_and_set |\n136\t| `claim_auto` | `atomic_subcommand` \\| `non_atomic_scan` | non_atomic_scan | atomic_subcommand | atomic_subcommand |\n137\t| `split` | `transactional_batch` \\| `sequential` | sequential | transactional_batch | sequential |\n138\t| create → ID | `bare_id` \\| `json_field` | bare_id | bare_id | bare_id |\n139\t| labels | `csv` \\| `repeated` | csv | repeated | repeated |\n140\t| `import` | `bare` \\| `input_plus_mode` | bare | bare | input_plus_mode |\n141\t\n142\tSix small enums cover every divergence found across three upstreams. NEEDLE implements each strategy **once**; a descriptor selects among them. A new CLI that fits the existing strategies is pure configuration. A new CLI that genuinely does something novel adds *one enum variant*, not a `BeadStore` impl — and that variant is then available to every backend.\n143\t\n144\tIllustrative descriptor (abridged):\n145\t\n146\t```yaml\n147\tname: beads_rust\n148\tbinary: br\n149\tdetect_paths: [\"~/.cargo/bin/br\"]\n150\tidentity_pattern: \"^br \"          # guards against the shim — see §3\n151\toperations:\n152\t  show:       { argv: [\"show\", \"{id}\", \"--json\"], parse: json_object }\n153\t  create:     { argv: [\"create\", \"--title\", \"{title}\", \"--body\", \"{body}\", \"--silent\"],\n154\t                labels: { style: csv, flag: \"--labels\" }, parse: bare_id }\n155\t  claim:      { strategy: compare_and_set,\n156\t                argv: [\"update\", \"{id}\", \"-s\", \"in_progress\", \"--assignee\", \"{actor}\"] }\n157\t  claim_auto: { strategy: non_atomic_scan }\n158\t  dep_add:    { argv: [\"dep\", \"add\", \"{blocked}\", \"{blocker}\", \"-t\", \"blocks\"] }\n159\t  split:      { strategy: sequential }\n160\tcapabilities: { atomic_claim: false, transactional_batch: false, velocity_metadata: false }\n161\t```\n162\t\n163\tThe `bf` descriptor differs only in data — `claim: { strategy: batch_op }`, `dep_add: [\"dep\",\"add\",\"{blocker}\",\"--blocks\",\"{blocked}\"]`, `capabilities.atomic_claim: true` — not in code.\n164\t\n165\t### 3. Identity is verified, never inferred\n166\t\n167\tEvery descriptor carries `identity_pattern`, checked against the resolved binary's `--version` output. `~/.local/bin/br` is a shim that `exec`s `bf`, so it reports `bf <version>` and fails the `beads_rust` descriptor's `^br ` check. This is the mechanism that makes §5's chimera impossible to reconstruct: a store can never bind to a binary speaking a different dialect, because binding requires the identity to match the descriptor that supplies the argv.\n168\t\n169\t### 4. Capabilities are declared and optionally probed\n170\t\n171\tDescriptors declare capabilities; where an upstream exposes a machine-readable contract (`bead capabilities --profile`, `bf schema`/`robot-docs`, `br schema`), probe at discovery and **reconcile against the declaration**, warning on mismatch. A declaration that drifts from reality is then visible rather than silently wrong — the failure mode of the bf 0.2.0 `--limit 0` workaround, which is still applied unconditionally at `:1357`/`:2094`.\n172\t\n173\t### 5. One `CliBeadStore`\n174\t\n175\tA single `BeadStore` impl driven by a `BeadBackend`. `BrCliBeadStore` and `BfCliBeadStore` are deleted; their behavior survives as the `beads_rust` and `bead-forge` builtin descriptors. This removes the chimera by construction rather than by repair: there is no store that can hold beads_rust argv and a bf binary at the same time.\n176\t\n177\t### 6. The rest follows\n178\t\n179\t- **One resolver.** `resolve_bead_cli()` returns a descriptor plus a verified path, replacing all five hardcoded chains (`:758-775`, `:1127-1136`, `:1893-1902`, `worker/mod.rs:732-742`, `cli/mod.rs:3626-3632`). Per-workspace via `.needle.yaml`.\n180\t- **`predispatch` goes through the store** (`validation/predispatch.rs:128` → `BeadStore::show`), removing the last non-trait call site.\n181\t- **Prompt fragments render from the active descriptor** (`prompt/mod.rs:56`, `:64`, `:294-325`), so the agent is told to run the binary that is present and the dialect is written down exactly once — in the descriptor.\n182\t- **`needle bead-backend <name>`**, mirroring the existing `needle test-agent`: resolve, verify identity, probe capabilities, print the resolved argv for each operation. A new descriptor is testable without dispatching a worker.\n183\t\n184\t### 7. Backend priority: bead-rs primary, bead-forge secondary, beads_rust tertiary, open world beyond\n185\t\n186\tOperator decision, 2026-08-12. Three consequences, none of which change the\n187\tmechanism above — the descriptor design was already priority-agnostic, which is\n188\twhy this is a sequencing and defaults decision rather than a redesign.\n189\t\n190\t**Sequencing inverts.** Phase 16 currently authors descriptors 16.4a beads_rust →\n191\t16.4b bead-forge → 16.4c bead-rs, so the primary backend lands last. Reorder to\n192\tbead-rs first. Its descriptor is also the only one that cannot be written from a\n193\treleased artifact — bead-rs is Forgejo-only with no GitHub releases and is under\n194\tactive development in agent-sandbox, so its `verified_against` names a commit and\n195\tmust be re-verified when that moves.\n196\t\n197\t**`auto` detection prefers `bead`, then `bf`, then `br`.** Today every discovery\n198\tchain resolves `bf` first, which is §5's defect in a different costume: the\n199\tdefault should express the intended ordering rather than whatever the fleet host\n200\thappens to have installed.\n201\t\n202\t**The primary backend is the weakest on two capabilities, and that must be\n203\tdeclared rather than discovered in production.** Re-probed against `bead` 0.1.1\n204\ton 2026-08-12 (the ADR's original evidence was `fa30574`, since superseded):\n205\t\n206\t- **No transactional `batch`.** `bf` remains the only backend that can make\n207\t  mitosis atomic. With bead-rs primary, `split` runs the `sequential` strategy\n208\t  for the default backend, so a SIGKILL, OOM, or pod eviction between child\n209\t  creation and dependency wiring leaves orphaned children — the exact hazard\n210\t  `bead_store` already documents for the non-atomic path. This is a real\n211\t  regression against the current bf default and belongs in 16.11's operator-facing\n212\t  capability-gap doc, not in a log line.\n213\t- **No velocity metadata on `claim`.** `bf claim` takes `--model --harness\n214\t  --harness-version`; `bead claim` does not. Telemetry that NEEDLE records today\n215\t  is simply absent for the primary backend.\n216\t\n217\tAgainst that, bead-rs is *stronger* where it matters most for fleet correctness,\n218\tand the priority decision buys these:\n219\t\n220\t- **Fenced, TTL'd leases** — `claim --lease-ttl --renew-lease --fencing-token`.\n221\t  This is a direct mechanism for the orphaned-claim class tracked in `bf-1e0`\n222\t  (\"Self-healing fleet: recover from worker death, exhaustion & orphaned\n223\t  claims\"); four NEEDLE beads were found on 2026-08-12 still assigned to workers\n224\t  that no longer exist. A TTL expires the claim without a janitor, and the\n225\t  fencing token stops a resurrected worker from writing after its lease lapsed.\n226\t- **Cycles rejected at insertion**, inside the transaction — the defect class\n227\t  that required a manual graph repair of this very workspace on 2026-08-12.\n228\t- **Readiness derived from the edge set**, with no stored `blocked` status to go\n229\t  stale, and the unfinished-blocker test embedded in the eligibility query so\n230\t  `ready` cannot disagree with the graph.\n231\t- `bead why` and `claim --why`, giving reason codes the other two cannot produce.\n232\t\n233\t**Two axes of interoperability, only one of which is on this critical path.**\n234\tWorth separating because they are easy to conflate:\n235\t\n236\t- *NEEDLE → any bead CLI* — this ADR. Needs descriptors and nothing else.\n237\t- *bead-rs ↔ other implementations' stored data* — bead-rs F012 profiles\n238\t  (`br-v1`, `bf-v1`), which `bead capabilities` currently reports as absent and\n239\t  which its own plan records as externally blocked on independently approved\n240\t  fixtures.\n241\t\n242\tMaking bead-rs NEEDLE's primary backend **does not depend on F012**. NEEDLE\n243\tdrives a CLI; it does not ask one backend to read another's store. Only\n244\tmigrating a workspace between backends needs the profiles.\n245\t\n246\t**The open-world row is the requirement that fixes the design.** \"Other bead\n247\tsystems that exist in the world\" is not satisfied by three good descriptors — it\n248\tis satisfied only if a fourth backend needs no NEEDLE change. That is the property\n249\t§1 and §2 deliver, and it is the reason the hardcoded-impl-per-upstream drafts are\n250\trejected rather than merely inelegant. Two obligations follow: the six strategy\n251\tenums must be treated as a published extension point rather than an internal\n252\tdetail, and capability negotiation (§4) is the discovery mechanism for a backend\n253\tnobody wrote a descriptor for — all three current backends already expose a\n254\tcapabilities-style surface, and bead-rs's is a full JSON contract\n255\t(`contract: native-v1`, `atomic_claim`, statuses, checkpoint formats, schema refs).\n256\t\n257\tMinor defect found while re-probing: `bead capabilities` reports\n258\t`\"version\": \"0.1.0\"` while `bead --version` reports `0.1.1`. A descriptor's\n259\t`verified_against` must read one of these deliberately, and the disagreement\n260\tshould be filed upstream.\n261\t\n262\t## Alternatives Considered\n263\t\n264\t- **One hardcoded `BeadStore` impl per upstream** (this ADR's first two drafts). Rejected on the operator's requirement: it hardcodes three harnesses, so a fourth bead CLI needs a Rust file, a code review, and a NEEDLE release. It also duplicates the ~20 operations three times, which is how the two existing impls drifted apart in the first place — `add_dependency` is correct in one and wrong in the other precisely because the same command is written twice. The strategy-enum design above answers the objection those drafts raised (that a flat argv table cannot express structural difference) without paying the duplication cost.\n265\t\n266\t- **A flat argv-template table with no strategies.** Rejected, and this was the correct objection in the earlier drafts — it just did not follow through to the fix. A table of argv strings cannot express \"claim is one atomic call here and a read-then-write there\", and papering over that would silently give beads_rust workspaces the race semantics of bead-forge. Strategies make the difference explicit and testable.\n267\t\n268\t- **Standardize on one CLI and drop the others.** Rejected on the operator's explicit requirement: all three upstreams are live and independently maintained. Note the `br` shim is itself part of the hazard — it makes `which br` return a binary that speaks `bf`, which is how §5 went unnoticed.\n269\t\n270\t- **A `bf`-compatible shim in the sandbox image translating to `bead`.** Rejected: buries the mismatch in an undocumented script on one image — the same shape as the shim that concealed §5 — and cannot express `batch`-shaped calls, since bead-rs has no equivalent.\n271\t\n272\t- **Teach the other CLIs a `batch` subcommand so one dialect works everywhere.** Scope inversion: makes two external roadmaps a blocker for NEEDLE portability, and leaves every other divergence unaddressed.\n273\t\n274\t- **Full scripting (Lua/Rhai/WASM) per backend.** Genuinely maximal configurability. Rejected as disproportionate: six enums cover every divergence observed across three independently-evolving upstreams plus their common Go ancestor, and a scripting runtime turns every bead operation into arbitrary user code on the path that claims and closes work.\n275\t\n276\t## Consequences\n277\t\n278\t- **A new bead CLI is a YAML file.** The three current backends stop being privileged: they are the shipped defaults, overridable by name like any agent adapter. This is the property the operator asked for and the first two drafts did not deliver.\n279\t- **The chimera becomes unconstructible.** Argv and binary come from the same descriptor, and identity is verified against it. §5's failure mode cannot recur by omission.\n280\t- **Duplication collapses.** ~20 operations currently written twice (soon three times) become one engine plus three data files. The `add_dependency` split-brain — right in one impl, wrong in the other — cannot happen when the command is written once per backend and nowhere else.\n281\t- **Atomic mitosis stays bf-only and atomic claim stays bf/bead-only.** The descriptor makes these gaps *declared and visible* rather than implicit in which impl you happened to construct, but it does not close them. `br` retains a real TOCTOU window between `ready` and `update` in `claim_auto` — two workers on one beads_rust workspace can claim the same bead. This is the duplicate-claim hazard CLAUDE.md already names as the real fleet failure mode, and it must be surfaced to operators, not just logged.\n282\t- **Strategy coverage is a real constraint.** A backend that fits no existing strategy needs an enum variant before its YAML works. That is the honest cost of not shipping a scripting runtime, and the failure is loud (unknown strategy → descriptor validation error) rather than silent.\n283\t- **Descriptor validation becomes load-bearing.** A malformed descriptor is now the way a fleet breaks. `load_bead_backends()` must reject unknown strategies, unresolvable placeholders, and missing required operations at load time, not at first claim — and `needle bead-backend <name>` must make that checkable before deployment.\n284\t- **The two existing impls are deleted, not refactored.** Their test suites must be re-expressed as descriptor conformance tests against the same fixture-CLI pattern (`:2809`, `:2858`, `:2960`), or coverage silently drops on the paths where a bug means duplicate dispatch or a lost bead.\n285\t\n286\t## Evidence\n287\t\n288\t- Installed binaries probed 2026-08-11: `~/.cargo/bin/br` → `br 0.1.28` (dicklesworthstone/beads_rust); `~/.local/bin/bf` → `bf 0.4.1` (jedarden/bead-forge); `~/go/bin/bd` → `bd 0.49.6` (Go beads, ancestor). `~/.local/bin/br` is a **shim** that logs the caller and `exec`s `bf` — so `which br` does not find beads_rust, which is how §5 stayed hidden.\n289\t- `br 0.1.28 create --help`: `-d, --description [aliases: --body]`, `-l, --labels` (comma-separated), `--silent`, `--json`. `br dep add --help`: `Usage: br dep add [OPTIONS] <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON>`, `-t, --type … [default: blocks]`. `br update --help`: `-s, --status`, `--assignee`, `--notes`. `br sync --help`: `--flush-only`, `--import-only` (both bare). `br --help`: no `claim`, no `batch`; has `ready`, `schema`.\n290\t- `bf 0.4.1 create --help`: `--title --description --type --priority --assignee --label --json --envelope --no-auto-flush --no-progress --workspace` — no `--body`, `--silent`, or `--labels`. `bf dep add --help`: `Usage: bf dep add [OPTIONS] <BLOCKER>` plus `--blocks <BLOCKS>`. Draft 1's proposed fix would have broken genuine beads_rust support. That objection was right about argv tables and wrong about the conclusion: a per-operation *strategy* enum parameterized by argv templates expresses the divergence exactly, and NEEDLE already runs this pattern for agent harnesses (`AgentAdapter` + `load_adapters`, `src/dispatch/mod.rs:570-660`) — a precedent both earlier drafts missed while proposing a parallel mechanism for the same problem one layer down.\n303\t- **2026-08-12, draft 4** — after the operator set the interop goal explicitly: **bead-rs primary, bead-forge secondary, beads_rust tertiary, and other bead systems that exist in the world.** The mechanism in drafts 1-3 needed no change; the data-driven design was already priority-agnostic, which is the evidence that draft 3 chose correctly. Phase 16 is now authorized work rather than a proposal the fleet was executing against ahead of a decision. It sets\nwhich backend the defaults favour and which descriptor is written first — it does\n**not** reduce the others to second-class. All three stay first-class, and the\nopen-world row is a requirement, not a courtesy: NEEDLE must be able to drive a\nbead CLI that did not exist when NEEDLE was compiled.\n\n(The original Go `beads` — `bd` v0.49.6, `~/go/bin/bd`, the common ancestor of all\nthree — is the nearest concrete instance of that fourth row, and is why the three\ndialects rhyme without matching.)\n\nThe immediate trigger is the `game-of-life` project in the **agent-sandbox** cluster, whose workspace is bead-rs-backed. Stock NEEDLE cannot drive it: a worker booted there fails at the first claim. But the investigation found the problem is broader than one missing backend, and that NEEDLE's *existing* handling of the two backends it nominally supports is already incorrect.\n\n### The seam is right; what leaks past it is not\n\n`trait BeadStore` (`src/bead_store/mod.rs:546`) already exists, is `Send + Sync`, and is what every consumer holds — `Arc<dyn BeadStore>` in `Worker` (`src/worker/mod.rs:306-308`), in `Claimer`, in every strand. Two impls already exist: `BrCliBeadStore` (`:701`) and `BfCliBeadStore` (`:1852`). Nothing in the worker or strand layer knows which CLI is underneath. **That part of the design is sound and does not change.**\n\nFour things leak past it.\n\n### 1. Binary resolution is hardcoded in five places, one of which bypasses the trait\n\n| Site | Behavior |\n|---|---|\n| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:758-775` | `BrCliBeadStore::discover` — chain `bf` → `~/.local/bin/bf` → `br` → `~/.local/bin/br` |\n| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:1127-1136` | a **second**, independent `resolve_bf()` used only by `run_bf_batch` / `run_bf_claim` |\n| `src/bead_store/mod.rs:1893-1902` | `BfCliBeadStore::discover` — a third copy |\n| `src/worker/mod.rs:732-742` | boot-time version handshake, `which::which(\"bf\")` inline |\n| `src/cli/mod.rs:3626-3632` | `needle doctor` preflight — `bf` else `br` else fail `\"no bead store CLI found on PATH (checked bf, br)\"` |\n| `src/validation/predispatch.rs:128` | `run(workspace, \"bf\", &[\"show\", …])` — **bypasses `BeadStore` altogether** |\n\nThe first row is the load-bearing defect. **`BrCliBeadStore::discover` resolves `bf` first** — so the store that speaks beads_rust dialect is bound, by default, to the bead-forge binary. See §5.\n\n### 2. Three dialects, diverged from a common ancestor in three directions\n\nEnumerated from each installed binary's own `--help` on 2026-08-11. This is the matrix any backend abstraction has to absorb:\n\n| Operation | `br` 0.1.28 | `bf` 0.4.1 | `bead` 0.1.0 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| atomic server-side claim | **absent** | `claim --model --harness --harness-version --assignee --json` | `claim --assignee --json --policy` (no velocity metadata) |\n| transactional batch | **absent** | `batch --json '[…]'` | **absent** |\n| create: description | `-d/--description` (**`--body` is a valid alias**) | `--description` only | `--description` only |\n| create: labels | `-l/--labels` **comma-separated** | repeated `--label` | repeated `--label` |\n| create: quiet ID | `--silent` | absent (bare ID on stdout) | absent (bare ID on stdout) |\n| `dep add` | `<ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t blocks` — **2 positionals** | `<BLOCKER> --blocks <BLOCKED> -t` — **1 positional** | `<BLOCKED> <BLOCKER> --kind blocks` — **2 positionals** |\n| `update --assignee` | present | **removed in 0.4.1** (`bf-1hmey`) | present, plus `--clear-assignee` |\n| `sync --import-only` | bare | bare | requires `--input` + one of `--restore-into-empty`/`--merge` |\n| ready frontier | `ready --json --limit` | `ready` | `list --ready` |\n| `doctor --repair` | present | present | present |\n| close reason | `-r/--reason` | `--reason` | `--reason` |\n| machine-readable contract | `schema`; **`capabilities` + `robot-docs` as of 0.2.22** | `schema`, `robot-docs` | `capabilities --profile` |\n\nTwo structural facts fall out. **`bf` is the only backend with a transactional `batch`**, so it is the only one that can make mitosis atomic. **`bf` is the only backend that dropped `update --assignee`**, so it is the only one that *needs* `batch` for something as ordinary as claiming. Those two facts are the same fact, and together they set the bar for any backend abstraction: the backends do not differ only in flag spelling, they differ in which operations are single commands at all. A configuration format that captures only argv cannot express that difference — which is why the Decision below pairs argv templates with a per-operation *strategy*.\n\nNote also that `dep add`'s positional order agrees between `br` and `bead` (blocked first, blocker second) and `bf` is the outlier. Getting this backwards inverts every dependency edge rather than failing loudly — the one place in this ADR where a wrong guess is worse than a crash.\n\n### 3. The prompt hands the agent a hardcoded dialect\n\n`src/prompt/mod.rs` embeds `bf update` (`:56`), `bf close` (`:64`), and a whole `bf create` / `bf show` / `bf dep add` / `bf label add` block in the mitosis-split instructions (`:294-325`), with a test asserting the literal string (`:1066-1067`). An agent in the bead-rs sandbox is told to run a binary that is not installed there.\n\n### 4. Version-handshake logic is bead-forge-specific\n\n`check_bead_forge_version` / `run_version_handshake` (`:295-419`) parse bead-forge version strings to detect bf 0.2.0's `--limit 0` bug. Against `br --version` or `bead --version` this degrades to a warning, but the `--limit 999999` workaround it exists to justify is applied unconditionally at `:1357` and `:2094`.\n\n### 5. `BrCliBeadStore` is a *correct* beads_rust store bound to the wrong binary\n\nThis is the finding that reframes the rest. Checked against the real `br` 0.1.28 at `~/.cargo/bin/br`:\n\n```\ncreate --title T --body B --json --silent --labels a,b      (:1550-1563)\ndep add <blocked> <blocker> --type blocks                   (:1579)\nsync --import-only                                          (:1706)\nlist --json --limit 999999                                  (:1357)\ndoctor --repair                                             (:1675)\n```\n\n**Every one of these is valid beads_rust.** `--body` is a documented alias of `-d/--description`; `--silent` exists; `-l/--labels` is comma-separated; `dep add` takes two positionals with `-t` defaulting to `blocks`; `sync --import-only` is bare; `list` has `--json` and `--limit`. `BrCliBeadStore` is not stale, drifted, or wrong. It is a faithful beads_rust adapter.\n\nThe defect is that **`discover()` (`:758-775`) resolves `bf` before `br`**, so on this host — and on every fleet host, where `~/.local/bin/bf` is present — the beads_rust adapter sends beads_rust argv to the bead-forge binary, which rejects most of it. `bf 0.4.1 create` has no `--body`, no `--silent`, no `--labels`. `bf 0.4.1 dep add` takes one positional, not two.\n\nCompounding it, bf-only calls were grafted *into* the beads_rust store: `claim` (`:1428-1437`), `release` (`:1479-1486`), and `split` (`:1485`, `:1508`) all route through `bf batch` via the second resolver at `:1127`, and `claim_auto` shells to `bf claim` (`:1194-1220`). beads_rust has neither subcommand. So `BrCliBeadStore` is now a chimera: beads_rust argv for create/dep/sync/list, bead-forge argv for claim/release/split, and a resolver that picks whichever binary it finds first regardless of which half is being invoked.\n\nThere is exactly one genuine argv bug, and it is in the *other* store: `BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency` (`:2288`) emits two positionals, which is correct for `br` and `bead` but wrong for `bf`.\n\n**Consequence in production:** every worker path constructs `BrCliBeadStore` — `worker/mod.rs:1385`, `supervisor/mod.rs:214`, `strand/explore.rs:71`/`:450`, `strand/splice.rs:747`/`:839`/`:999`. `BfCliBeadStore` is built only in `cli/mod.rs:997` and `:3384`. So the fleet runs the chimera. `create_bead` fails with a clap parse error against `bf`, and through the trait's default `split_bead` (`:646-668`) that takes all of mitosis child creation with it.\n\n### 6. Descriptors must pin the version they were verified against\n\nThe `br` binary installed on this host is **v0.1.28, built 2026-03-29**. Upstream beads_rust is at **v0.2.22 (2026-08-06)** — roughly twenty releases and four months ahead. Every dialect fact in §2 was originally derived from the stale local binary.\n\nDownloading `br-0.2.22-linux_x86_64` from the GitHub release and re-probing confirms the dialect is stable across that gap on every point NEEDLE touches: `-d/--description` still carries `[alias: --body]`, `-l/--labels` is still comma-separated, `--silent` survives, `dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t` still takes two positionals, `update -s --assignee` is still present, and there is still no `claim` and no `batch`. That is luck, not design — and it is exactly the check a descriptor should force rather than leave to chance.\n\n0.2.22 does add subcommands: `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `capacity`, `coordination`, `gate`, `scheduler`, `vcs-status`. The first two matter here — **all three backends expose a capabilities-style contract surface**, so §4's negotiation is uniform rather than a bead-rs special case.\n\nTwo consequences for the design:\n\n- A descriptor carries `verified_against` (binary version) and the date it was checked. A fleet host running v0.1.28 while upstream ships v0.2.22 is normal; a descriptor that does not say which one it was written for is a guess.\n- **bead-rs is under active development in agent-sandbox**, so its surface is a *moving* target, not a stale one: the local `~/bead-rs` is nine commits past the `fa30574` this ADR cites, including `20853cf`, which fixed a defect that bricked every fresh clone. Its descriptor must be verified against the binary the sandbox actually runs, and re-verified when that moves. Unlike `br` and `bf`, bead-rs publishes **no GitHub releases** — it is Forgejo-only — so there is no release artifact to pin to and the descriptor must name a commit.\n\n## Decision\n\n**One descriptor-driven `CliBeadStore`, with backends defined as data — not one hardcoded impl per upstream.**\n\nNEEDLE already solves this exact problem for AI agent harnesses and the bead layer should not invent a second answer. `AgentAdapter` (`src/dispatch/mod.rs`) is a serde struct; `load_adapters` (`:607-660`) merges `builtin_adapters()` (`:570-579`) with user YAML dropped in `~/.config/needle/adapters/`, user files overriding built-ins by name. Adding a new agent harness requires no recompile. The bead CLI gets the same shape.\n\n### 1. `BeadBackend` descriptors, loaded like adapters\n\nA `BeadBackend` is a serde struct describing one CLI: binary name, identity check, detection paths, per-operation argv templates, and a declared capability set. `builtin_bead_backends()` ships `beads_rust`, `bead-forge`, and `bead-rs` as **data, not code**; `load_bead_backends()` merges user YAML from `~/.config/needle/bead-backends/`, overriding built-ins by name. `bead_cli.backend` in config names one; `auto` detects.\n\nA fourth CLI — `bd`, a fork, a future tool — is a YAML file. No recompile, no NEEDLE release.\n\n### 2. Structural divergence is expressed as a *strategy* per operation, not as argv alone\n\nThis is the part a flat argv table cannot do, and the reason the first two drafts of this ADR reached for hardcoded impls. The backends differ in **which operations are single commands at all**: `bf` claims via one transactional `batch` because it has no `update --assignee`; `br` and `bead` claim via a plain `update`; `br` has no server-side `claim`, so `claim_auto` there is a two-step read-then-write with different race properties.\n\nSo each operation declares a strategy drawn from a small closed set, parameterized by argv templates:\n\n| Operation | Strategies | `br` | `bf` | `bead` |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `claim` | `compare_and_set` \\| `batch_op` | compare_and_set | batch_op | compare_and_set |\n| `claim_auto` | `atomic_subcommand` \\| `non_atomic_scan` | non_atomic_scan | atomic_subcommand | atomic_subcommand |\n| `split` | `transactional_batch` \\| `sequential` | sequential | transactional_batch | sequential |\n| create → ID | `bare_id` \\| `json_field` | bare_id | bare_id | bare_id |\n| labels | `csv` \\| `repeated` | csv | repeated | repeated |\n| `import` | `bare` \\| `input_plus_mode` | bare | bare | input_plus_mode |\n\nSix small enums cover every divergence found across three upstreams. NEEDLE implements each strategy **once**; a descriptor selects among them. A new CLI that fits the existing strategies is pure configuration. A new CLI that genuinely does something novel adds *one enum variant*, not a `BeadStore` impl — and that variant is then available to every backend.\n\nIllustrative descriptor (abridged):\n\n```yaml\nname: beads_rust\nbinary: br\ndetect_paths: [\"~/.cargo/bin/br\"]\nidentity_pattern: \"^br \"          # guards against the shim — see §3\noperations:\n  show:       { argv: [\"show\", \"{id}\", \"--json\"], parse: json_object }\n  create:     { argv: [\"create\", \"--title\", \"{title}\", \"--body\", \"{body}\", \"--silent\"],\n                labels: { style: csv, flag: \"--labels\" }, parse: bare_id }\n  claim:      { strategy: compare_and_set,\n                argv: [\"update\", \"{id}\", \"-s\", \"in_progress\", \"--assignee\", \"{actor}\"] }\n  claim_auto: { strategy: non_atomic_scan }\n  dep_add:    { argv: [\"dep\", \"add\", \"{blocked}\", \"{blocker}\", \"-t\", \"blocks\"] }\n  split:      { strategy: sequential }\ncapabilities: { atomic_claim: false, transactional_batch: false, velocity_metadata: false }\n```\n\nThe `bf` descriptor differs only in data — `claim: { strategy: batch_op }`, `dep_add: [\"dep\",\"add\",\"{blocker}\",\"--blocks\",\"{blocked}\"]`, `capabilities.atomic_claim: true` — not in code.\n\n### 3. Identity is verified, never inferred\n\nEvery descriptor carries `identity_pattern`, checked against the resolved binary's `--version` output. `~/.local/bin/br` is a shim that `exec`s `bf`, so it reports `bf <version>` and fails the `beads_rust` descriptor's `^br ` check. This is the mechanism that makes §5's chimera impossible to reconstruct: a store can never bind to a binary speaking a different dialect, because binding requires the identity to match the descriptor that supplies the argv.\n\n### 4. Capabilities are declared and optionally probed\n\nDescriptors declare capabilities; where an upstream exposes a machine-readable contract (`bead capabilities --profile`, `bf schema`/`robot-docs`, `br schema`), probe at discovery and **reconcile against the declaration**, warning on mismatch. A declaration that drifts from reality is then visible rather than silently wrong — the failure mode of the bf 0.2.0 `--limit 0` workaround, which is still applied unconditionally at `:1357`/`:2094`.\n\n### 5. One `CliBeadStore`\n\nA single `BeadStore` impl driven by a `BeadBackend`. `BrCliBeadStore` and `BfCliBeadStore` are deleted; their behavior survives as the `beads_rust` and `bead-forge` builtin descriptors. This removes the chimera by construction rather than by repair: there is no store that can hold beads_rust argv and a bf binary at the same time.\n\n### 6. The rest follows\n\n- **One resolver.** `resolve_bead_cli()` returns a descriptor plus a verified path, replacing all five hardcoded chains (`:758-775`, `:1127-1136`, `:1893-1902`, `worker/mod.rs:732-742`, `cli/mod.rs:3626-3632`). Per-workspace via `.needle.yaml`.\n- **`predispatch` goes through the store** (`validation/predispatch.rs:128` → `BeadStore::show`), removing the last non-trait call site.\n- **Prompt fragments render from the active descriptor** (`prompt/mod.rs:56`, `:64`, `:294-325`), so the agent is told to run the binary that is present and the dialect is written down exactly once — in the descriptor.\n- **`needle bead-backend <name>`**, mirroring the existing `needle test-agent`: resolve, verify identity, probe capabilities, print the resolved argv for each operation. A new descriptor is testable without dispatching a worker.\n\n### 7. Backend priority: bead-rs primary, bead-forge secondary, beads_rust tertiary, open world beyond\n\nOperator decision, 2026-08-12. Three consequences, none of which change the\nmechanism above — the descriptor design was already priority-agnostic, which is\nwhy this is a sequencing and defaults decision rather than a redesign.\n\n**Sequencing inverts.** Phase 16 currently authors descriptors 16.4a beads_rust →\n16.4b bead-forge → 16.4c bead-rs, so the primary backend lands last. Reorder to\nbead-rs first. Its descriptor is also the only one that cannot be written from a\nreleased artifact — bead-rs is Forgejo-only with no GitHub releases and is under\nactive development in agent-sandbox, so its `verified_against` names a commit and\nmust be re-verified when that moves.\n\n**`auto` detection prefers `bead`, then `bf`, then `br`.** Today every discovery\nchain resolves `bf` first, which is §5's defect in a different costume: the\ndefault should express the intended ordering rather than whatever the fleet host\nhappens to have installed.\n\n**The primary backend is the weakest on two capabilities, and that must be\ndeclared rather than discovered in production.** Re-probed against `bead` 0.1.1\non 2026-08-12 (the ADR's original evidence was `fa30574`, since superseded):\n\n- **No transactional `batch`.** `bf` remains the only backend that can make\n  mitosis atomic. With bead-rs primary, `split` runs the `sequential` strategy\n  for the default backend, so a SIGKILL, OOM, or pod eviction between child\n  creation and dependency wiring leaves orphaned children — the exact hazard\n  `bead_store` already documents for the non-atomic path. This is a real\n  regression against the current bf default and belongs in 16.11's operator-facing\n  capability-gap doc, not in a log line.\n- **No velocity metadata on `claim`.** `bf claim` takes `--model --harness\n  --harness-version`; `bead claim` does not. Telemetry that NEEDLE records today\n  is simply absent for the primary backend.\n\nAgainst that, bead-rs is *stronger* where it matters most for fleet correctness,\nand the priority decision buys these:\n\n- **Fenced, TTL'd leases** — `claim --lease-ttl --renew-lease --fencing-token`.\n  This is a direct mechanism for the orphaned-claim class tracked in `bf-1e0`\n  (\"Self-healing fleet: recover from worker death, exhaustion & orphaned\n  claims\"); four NEEDLE beads were found on 2026-08-12 still assigned to workers\n  that no longer exist. A TTL expires the claim without a janitor, and the\n  fencing token stops a resurrected worker from writing after its lease lapsed.\n- **Cycles rejected at insertion**, inside the transaction — the defect class\n  that required a manual graph repair of this very workspace on 2026-08-12.\n- **Readiness derived from the edge set**, with no stored `blocked` status to go\n  stale, and the unfinished-blocker test embedded in the eligibility query so\n  `ready` cannot disagree with the graph.\n- `bead why` and `claim --why`, giving reason codes the other two cannot produce.\n\n**Two axes of interoperability, only one of which is on this critical path.**\nWorth separating because they are easy to conflate:\n\n- *NEEDLE → any bead CLI* — this ADR. Needs descriptors and nothing else.\n- *bead-rs ↔ other implementations' stored data* — bead-rs F012 profiles\n  (`br-v1`, `bf-v1`), which `bead capabilities` currently reports as absent and\n  which its own plan records as externally blocked on independently approved\n  fixtures.\n\nMaking bead-rs NEEDLE's primary backend **does not depend on F012**. NEEDLE\ndrives a CLI; it does not ask one backend to read another's store. Only\nmigrating a workspace between backends needs the profiles.\n\n**The open-world row is the requirement that fixes the design.** \"Other bead\nsystems that exist in the world\" is not satisfied by three good descriptors — it\nis satisfied only if a fourth backend needs no NEEDLE change. That is the property\n§1 and §2 deliver, and it is the reason the hardcoded-impl-per-upstream drafts are\nrejected rather than merely inelegant. Two obligations follow: the six strategy\nenums must be treated as a published extension point rather than an internal\ndetail, and capability negotiation (§4) is the discovery mechanism for a backend\nnobody wrote a descriptor for — all three current backends already expose a\ncapabilities-style surface, and bead-rs's is a full JSON contract\n(`contract: native-v1`, `atomic_claim`, statuses, checkpoint formats, schema refs).\n\nMinor defect found while re-probing: `bead capabilities` reports\n`\"version\": \"0.1.0\"` while `bead --version` reports `0.1.1`. A descriptor's\n`verified_against` must read one of these deliberately, and the disagreement\nshould be filed upstream.\n\n## Alternatives Considered\n\n- **One hardcoded `BeadStore` impl per upstream** (this ADR's first two drafts). Rejected on the operator's requirement: it hardcodes three harnesses, so a fourth bead CLI needs a Rust file, a code review, and a NEEDLE release. It also duplicates the ~20 operations three times, which is how the two existing impls drifted apart in the first place — `add_dependency` is correct in one and wrong in the other precisely because the same command is written twice. The strategy-enum design above answers the objection those drafts raised (that a flat argv table cannot express structural difference) without paying the duplication cost.\n\n- **A flat argv-template table with no strategies.** Rejected, and this was the correct objection in the earlier drafts — it just did not follow through to the fix. A table of argv strings cannot express \"claim is one atomic call here and a read-then-write there\", and papering over that would silently give beads_rust workspaces the race semantics of bead-forge. Strategies make the difference explicit and testable.\n\n- **Standardize on one CLI and drop the others.** Rejected on the operator's explicit requirement: all three upstreams are live and independently maintained. Note the `br` shim is itself part of the hazard — it makes `which br` return a binary that speaks `bf`, which is how §5 went unnoticed.\n\n- **A `bf`-compatible shim in the sandbox image translating to `bead`.** Rejected: buries the mismatch in an undocumented script on one image — the same shape as the shim that concealed §5 — and cannot express `batch`-shaped calls, since bead-rs has no equivalent.\n\n- **Teach the other CLIs a `batch` subcommand so one dialect works everywhere.** Scope inversion: makes two external roadmaps a blocker for NEEDLE portability, and leaves every other divergence unaddressed.\n\n- **Full scripting (Lua/Rhai/WASM) per backend.** Genuinely maximal configurability. Rejected as disproportionate: six enums cover every divergence observed across three independently-evolving upstreams plus their common Go ancestor, and a scripting runtime turns every bead operation into arbitrary user code on the path that claims and closes work.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- **A new bead CLI is a YAML file.** The three current backends stop being privileged: they are the shipped defaults, overridable by name like any agent adapter. This is the property the operator asked for and the first two drafts did not deliver.\n- **The chimera becomes unconstructible.** Argv and binary come from the same descriptor, and identity is verified against it. §5's failure mode cannot recur by omission.\n- **Duplication collapses.** ~20 operations currently written twice (soon three times) become one engine plus three data files. The `add_dependency` split-brain — right in one impl, wrong in the other — cannot happen when the command is written once per backend and nowhere else.\n- **Atomic mitosis stays bf-only and atomic claim stays bf/bead-only.** The descriptor makes these gaps *declared and visible* rather than implicit in which impl you happened to construct, but it does not close them. `br` retains a real TOCTOU window between `ready` and `update` in `claim_auto` — two workers on one beads_rust workspace can claim the same bead. This is the duplicate-claim hazard CLAUDE.md already names as the real fleet failure mode, and it must be surfaced to operators, not just logged.\n- **Strategy coverage is a real constraint.** A backend that fits no existing strategy needs an enum variant before its YAML works. That is the honest cost of not shipping a scripting runtime, and the failure is loud (unknown strategy → descriptor validation error) rather than silent.\n- **Descriptor validation becomes load-bearing.** A malformed descriptor is now the way a fleet breaks. `load_bead_backends()` must reject unknown strategies, unresolvable placeholders, and missing required operations at load time, not at first claim — and `needle bead-backend <name>` must make that checkable before deployment.\n- **The two existing impls are deleted, not refactored.** Their test suites must be re-expressed as descriptor conformance tests against the same fixture-CLI pattern (`:2809`, `:2858`, `:2960`), or coverage silently drops on the paths where a bug means duplicate dispatch or a lost bead.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Installed binaries probed 2026-08-11: `~/.cargo/bin/br` → `br 0.1.28` (dicklesworthstone/beads_rust); `~/.local/bin/bf` → `bf 0.4.1` (jedarden/bead-forge); `~/go/bin/bd` → `bd 0.49.6` (Go beads, ancestor). `~/.local/bin/br` is a **shim** that logs the caller and `exec`s `bf` — so `which br` does not find beads_rust, which is how §5 stayed hidden.\n- `br 0.1.28 create --help`: `-d, --description [aliases: --body]`, `-l, --labels` (comma-separated), `--silent`, `--json`. `br dep add --help`: `Usage: br dep add [OPTIONS] <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON>`, `-t, --type … [default: blocks]`. `br update --help`: `-s, --status`, `--assignee`, `--notes`. `br sync --help`: `--flush-only`, `--import-only` (both bare). `br --help`: no `claim`, no `batch`; has `ready`, `schema`.\n- `bf 0.4.1 create --help`: `--title --description --type --priority --assignee --label --json --envelope --no-auto-flush --no-progress --workspace` — no `--body`, `--silent`, or `--labels`. `bf dep add --help`: `Usage: bf dep add [OPTIONS] <BLOCKER>` plus `--blocks <BLOCKS>`. Verified empirically: `bf dep add bf-46m05 --blocks bf-2qm6r` → `Added dependency: bf-2qm6r depends on bf-46m05 (blocks)`. `bf --help`: has `ready`, `claim`, `batch`, `schema`, `robot-docs`.\n- `bead` 0.1.0 surface from `~/bead-rs/src/cli.rs` @ `fa30574`: `Command` enum `:47-131` (no `batch`), `CreateOptions` `:181` (`--description`, repeated `--label`, no `--json`), `ListOptions` `:241` (`--json`, `--ready`, `--limit` 0-999999), `ClaimOptions` `:370` (no model/harness flags), `UpdateOptions` `:444` (**has** `--assignee` and `--clear-assignee`), `SyncCommand` `:667` (`--import-only` requires `--input` + `--restore-into-empty`|`--merge`), `DepAddOptions` `:975` (`--kind`), `DoctorOptions` `:1059`, `CapabilitiesOptions` `:1116`.\n- NEEDLE call sites: resolution `:758-775`, `:1127-1136`, `:1893-1902`, `worker/mod.rs:732-742`, `cli/mod.rs:3626-3632`, `validation/predispatch.rs:128`. beads_rust-dialect argv in `BrCliBeadStore`: `:1357`, `:1550-1563`, `:1579`, `:1675`, `:1706`. Diagnosed `BrCliBeadStore`'s `--body`/`--silent`/`--labels` and two-positional `dep add` as stale drift to be rewritten toward the bf dialect.\n- **2026-08-11, draft 2** — after the operator required first-class support for all three upstreams. Probing the real `~/.cargo/bin/br` (which `which br` does not find, because a shim shadows it) showed that argv is **correct beads_rust**, and the actual defect is `discover()` binding that store to the `bf` binary, plus bf-only `batch`/`claim` calls grafted into it. Draft 1's proposed fix would have broken genuine beads_rust support. Only one real argv bug survived: `BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency` (`:2288`).\n- **2026-08-11, draft 3 (current)** — after the operator required the bead-CLI component be genuinely configurable rather than hardcoding harnesses for three named CLIs. Drafts 1 and 2 both landed on one Rust impl per upstream, and draft 2 explicitly argued against a data-driven design on the grounds that an argv table cannot express structural divergence. That objection was right about argv tables and wrong about the conclusion: a per-operation *strategy* enum parameterized by argv templates expresses the divergence exactly, and NEEDLE already runs this pattern for agent harnesses (`AgentAdapter` + `load_adapters`, `src/dispatch/mod.rs:570-660`) — a precedent both earlier drafts missed while proposing a parallel mechanism for the same problem one layer down.\n- **2026-08-12, draft 4** — after the operator set the interop goal explicitly: **bead-rs primary, bead-forge secondary, beads_rust tertiary, and other bead systems that exist in the world.** The mechanism in drafts 1-3 needed no change; the data-driven design was already priority-agnostic, which is the evidence that draft 3 chose correctly. What changed is §7: descriptor authoring order inverts so the primary backend is written first rather than last, `auto` detection prefers `bead` over the incumbent `bf`, and the primary backend's two capability gaps (no transactional `batch`, no velocity metadata on claim) become declared operator-facing facts instead of surprises — non-atomic mitosis is a real regression against today's bf default. Re-probed `bead` 0.1.1 rather than trusting draft 3's `fa30574` evidence, which surfaced the fenced-lease claim surface (`--lease-ttl`/`--renew-lease`/`--fencing-token`) that drafts 1-3 did not know existed and that bears directly on `bf-1e0`. Also separated the two interop axes: NEEDLE→CLI (this ADR) does not depend on bead-rs F012 profiles, which `bead capabilities` reports as absent and which bead-rs's own plan records as externally blocked. The open-world row is promoted from an incidental benefit to a stated requirement, which makes the six strategy enums a published extension point rather than an internal detail.\n- **2026-08-12, accepted.** Operator accepted the decision as written in draft 4. Phase 16 is now authorized work rather than a proposal the fleet was executing against ahead of a decision. The staged-rollout item (`bf-4rdm5`) is load-bearing on the way in: this ADR changes the claim path for every backend, and NEEDLE's own coordination substrate is one of the workspaces being migrated.\n","numLines":305,"startLine":1,"totalLines":305}}}
